intro.title: Build typed backoff strategy interface
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed TypeScript interface for a backoff strategy, which is a common pattern for handling retries in network requests or operations that may fail. You will learn how to define a contract using TypeScript interfaces to specify the structure and types for backoff properties like delay and max attempts. The core concept involves using TypeScript's interface system to enforce type safety and ensure your strategy objects have the correct shape. You'll work with basic TypeScript constructs like interfaces, optional properties, and number types to create a reusable and reliable backoff strategy definition.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, typed backoff strategies are essential for handling API rate limiting and network instability in production systems. For example, when a dashboard fetches analytics data from a third-party service like Stripe or GitHub API, exponential backoff with jitter prevents overwhelming their servers during temporary outages. E-commerce platforms use typed backoff interfaces when retrying payment processing after declined transactions, ensuring type-safe configuration of delay intervals and maximum attempts. This pattern also appears in mobile apps that synchronize data with cloud services, where developers need compile-time guarantees about retry logic parameters to prevent runtime errors during intermittent connectivity.
